title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.03622v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) hold promise for zero-shot video task-progress estimation in robot learning, yet existing frameworks frequently suffer from confirmation bias, hallucinating progress in failed executions due to implicit success assumptions or relative temporal ranking designs. Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they demand expensive real-world robotics data and require computationally intensive post-training for every individual base model. To resolve these limitations, we introduce D&A (Describe & Assess): our approach decouples progress estimation into an objective, task-grounded textual description of scene dynamics followed by an assessment phase using explicit rubrics. By compelling the VLM to synthesize an explicit, text-based definition

translated_title: D&A：解耦描述与评估使视觉语言模型成为零样本机器人奖励模型
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）在机器人学习中的零样本视频任务进度估计方面展现出巨大前景，然而现有框架常常受到确认偏差的困扰，由于隐含的成功假设或相对时间排序设计，会在失败的执行过程中幻觉出任务进度。对前沿模型进行朴素提示会退化为一个二元成功检测器，无法捕捉细微的、非线性的进度变化与失败情况。虽然后训练方法可以通过显式训练缓解这一问题，但它们需要昂贵的真实世界机器人数据，并且需要对每个单独的基础模型进行计算密集型的后训练。为了解决这些局限性，我们提出了D&A（描述与评估）：我们的方法将进度估计解耦为两个阶段——首先对场景动态进行客观的、基于任务的文本描述，随后使用显式评分标准进行评估。通过迫使VLM综合生成一个显式的、基于文本的定义……
tldr: 提出D&A方法，将任务进度估计解耦为客观的场景描述与基于显式评分标准的评估两个阶段，使视觉语言模型无需昂贵后训练即可作为零样本机器人奖励模型，并有效避免确认偏差问题。
en_tdlr: D&A decouples task-progress estimation into an objective scene description phase followed by rubric-based assessment, enabling VLMs to serve as zero-shot robotic reward models without costly post-training while mitigating confirmation bias.
